about: The Debug page's API (window.QCCD_DEBUG, qccd/site/debug/debug.js), declared: every verb an agent's `debug` page action may call, and nothing else. The same verbs work on the Debug page and on every Studio page (where the first verb opens the panel beside the program). Each verb takes ONE object of arguments and returns JSON or a promise of it. Steps count from 1, as the Studio's status line does ("Step 7 / 11" is step 7). kind: read (changes nothing), view (changes what is shown: the step, the watch list, the crosses), load (opens another program in the page), run (computes: rules, conditions, expressions -- the grader's own rule language, in the page). A verb added to QCCD_DEBUG without an entry here, or an entry naming none, fails tests/test_agent_interface.py.

about.does: what the page is, every verb with what it does, and how steps are numbered

sources.does: the programs the page can open: every Studio page of the website (title, group, path), the person's saved design if there is one; filtered by words

args.q: words that must all appear in the title or path (optional)

open.does: open a program: a site page by the path `sources` gives (e.g. board/surface3_mem/02_ring16.html), 'design' for the design the person last left on the Design page, or 'studio' for a blank Design page; on the Debug page it loads into the frame and resolves with a summary, on a Studio page it goes to that page, where the debugger opens beside its program

status.does: where the debugger is (the Debug page, or beside this Studio page's program, and whether its panel is open), what is open (title, path, steps), the current step, the watch list, the rule set and whether the program was checked, which rules fail, and whether Python is loaded

goto.does: show a step (the Studio's animation seeks to it; the crosses and every panel follow)

args.step: 1 to the number of steps; -1 is the last

step.does: move forward or back by some steps from the current one

state.does: the state after a step: the instruction and what it did, the ions that moved, places over capacity, the hottest ions' n-bar, what you watch, and the rule failures crossed out there

watch.does: highlight and follow ions, sites, junctions or rails on the picture (each in its own colour, ions with a trail); isolate dims every other ion

trace.does: everything that happened to one ion, site, junction or rail, step by step: only the steps where something did (where it was, what acted on it, who was in it)

check.does: judge the program by a rule set the website ships and/or your own assertions (the rule language of the Rules page), locate every failure and cross it out on the picture; resolves with each rule's verdict and its first failures (step, places, the grader's sentence)

args.rules: a rule set's name (standard, cyclone, jones, ...), the text of one, or 'none'
args.assertions: your own rules: formulas, one per paragraph, optionally led by assert "title":, or rule-file text

failures.does: the located failures of the last check: rule, steps (from, until), places, message

next_failure.does: go to the next step where a shown rule starts failing

prev_failure.does: go to the previous step where a shown rule starts failing

find.does: a conditional breakpoint: the first step after the current one (before it, backward) at which a condition holds, written in the rule language over the instant t, e.g. occupancy("C3", t) > 1; goes there unless go is false

value.does: watch expressions: terms of the rule language evaluated at a step, with t the instant after it, e.g. occupancy("C0", t) or position("q3", t)

breakpoints.does: set what Continue stops at: steps, conditions (rule language over t), a rule starting to fail, something watched changing; returns them

continue.does: run forward (or backward) from the current step to the next breakpoint, and say what stopped it

report.does: a bug report of what the page shows: the program, the rules and their failures, the current step's state, the watch list, and a link that reopens the page exactly here, as Markdown and as data

link.does: the link that reopens the page on this program, at this step, with these rules, assertions and watch list
